title.narrative: Strengthening our unity through networking and advocacy (SOUTNA), Tatweer phase III

description.narrative:
Direct Beneficiaries: 180 civil society organisations enrolled in the SOUTNA programme across four Iraqi governorates — 20 organisations per governorate per programme cycle. Organisations are pre-classified into three categories reflecting their institutional maturity:
Category A (Established NGOs): Formally registered, 5+ years of operation, multi-donor experience Category B (Growing CBOs): Registered, 2–5 years, limited systems, local community focus Category C (Emerging CBOs): Newly registered or informally operating, strong community presence but limited institutional capacity
Selection deliberately prioritises diversity: women-led organisations, youth-led groups, organisations serving minority communities, disability-focused organisations, and grassroots entities that are typically excluded from international development programming due to registration or documentation barriers. Indirect Beneficiaries: An estimated 150,000 community members across Baghdad, Erbil, Basra, and Mosul/Ninawa who are directly served by the 180 participating organisations through their programmes, advocacy activities, and community services. Government stakeholders — including the Federal Directorate of NGOs and the KRG Directorate of NGOs — benefit through the Steering Committee engagement and the certification framework, which strengthens the government-civil society relationship and aligns with national civil society development priorities.

Iraq's civil society sector comprises over 6,000 registered organisations, yet the vast majority remain institutionally fragile ,lacking functional governance structures, financial management systems, and the organisational capacity needed to operate independently and sustainably. The sector is further constrained by shrinking civic space, increasing regulatory pressure, limited access to diversified funding, and the enduring effects of conflict and displacement ,particularly in Mosul and Ninawa governorate.
Cordaid has been working with Iraqi civil society since 2015 through the Tatweer Phase I and Phase II programmes, which demonstrated both the significant potential of local organisations and the critical need for sustained, structured institutional support ,rather than episodic training interventions. SOUTNA (Strengthening Our Unity Through Networking and Advocacy) is the third and most comprehensive phase of this investment, building directly on the lessons and relationships established through Tatweer.
SOUTNA responds to three interconnected gaps: weak institutional governance and systems among civil society organisations; limited advocacy capacity and access to policy dialogue; and insufficient investment in youth engagement in civic life. The programme operates across four strategically selected governorates — Baghdad, Erbil, Basra, and Mosul/Ninawa ,each representing a distinct civil society ecosystem with specific needs, contexts, and opportunities for impact.
The programme is funded by the European Union under Grant Contract NDICI-THE-MENA/2025/488-422 and implemented by Stichting Cordaid.

Overall Objective: To strengthen Iraqi civil society organisations as independent, credible, and sustainable actors of good governance and development, capable of effectively representing their constituencies and engaging in national and local policy processes. Specific Objectives: Output 1 Institutional Strengthening: To improve the institutional governance, operational capacity, and organisational resilience of 180 civil society organisations across four Iraqi governorates through a structured, 24-month capacity development journey including participatory assessment, co-created improvement planning, training, coaching, and certification. Output 2 Advocacy and Policy Engagement: To strengthen the advocacy capacity and policy influence of Iraqi CSOs, enabling them to effectively represent their constituencies in local and national governance processes, through training, advocacy grants, multi-stakeholder platforms, and the development of a context-specific Iraqi CSO Advocacy Playbook. Output 3 Youth Engagement and Leadership: To increase the meaningful participation of young people in civic life and civil society leadership, through targeted outreach to youth-led groups, leadership training, community grants, and structured youth networking.
